status: planned; no revised Issue 5 illustrations approved
wardrobe: Q retains Chapter Four's fitted sponsor jacket and small silver question mark. Preserve the established segmented oval head, ears, neck, long articulated limbs and underlying breastplate. No new knightly costume or unexplained return to the original torn coat.
secondary_character_design: Candelaria: small older Mexican forest worker, wool shawl and polished wooden staff; contemporary practical clothes, no invented ceremonial regalia. Establish distinct recurring designs for Lidia, her mother, the watering girl and mother, the grieving schoolgirl, Micaela, Celestina, Tere, the teacher, foundation director and assistant. These people are not interchangeable indigenous symbols. Match Micaela's later scenes before approving her design. Vero is the student who asks permission and records different vendor choices; her male partner carries the tally and tables. Do not render them as unauthorized photographers from the deleted version. The uncle's song scene is an afternoon broadcast, not automatically dusk.
art_direction: One unique scene from each exact facing page. Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, pure white highlights, no sepia paper texture. Full bleed at comic trim with separately typeset margin captions. Eastern Michoacan oyamel forest, contemporary local work and varied residents. No invented museum, school or reserve portrayed as an identified real institution. Preserve visual identity across the sequence.
approval_scope: Pagination and exact facing-scene plan only. The 44-page internal proof contains no illustrations. All assets remain planned and cannot be used for a final illustrated build until generated, inspected and hash-bound.

plates.caption: The Butterflies Have No General
plates.scene_brief: Wide vertical forest composition: Q in his fitted jacket on a narrow oyamel path, seen from behind beneath immense boughs clustered with monarchs. Candelaria leads farther along the path; a small group follows without cameras. Keep scale and physical place, not a messianic machine worshipped by butterflies. Quiet upper space for separately typeset cover title.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Five: The
Butterflies Have No
General
The invitation to Michoacán arrived
in the form of a holographic
butterfly.
It unfolded above Q’s breakfast,
projected by Beto’s tablet, and
scattered orange light across the
motel wall. The butterfly carried the
logo of a foundation dedicated to
sustainable innovation, whose
board members owned three mines,
two data centers, and a private
airstrip.
“They want you to visit the
monarch reserve,” Beto said.
“There will be cameras,
schoolchildren, and a statement
about the future.”
“Whose future?” Chano asked.
“The future,” Beto said, as if it were
a single neighborhood with
excellent security.
Q read the itinerary beneath the
projection. “Is this a visit to the
forest or a recording session with a
forest in it?”
“Both.”
“Then I want the guide to have the
last word about where we go.”
Beto agreed, provided the last word
could be recorded.
Before leaving, Q sent the
Custodian the corrected manuscript
pages and a proposed date for the
next call. He also followed up on
the petition's address query. The
answer still required a document
from Castalia. He could initiate
another journey more easily than
obtain proof of where the first had
begun.
They drove southeast toward the
mountains of eastern Michoacán.
Fields gave way to hills and pine
woods, then to the colder heights of
the oyamel forest. Along the road,
painted signs advertised trout,
cabins, meals, and land for sale to
people who wanted a piece of
wilderness without meeting its
neighbors.
The foundation had arranged a
convoy: two electric SUVs, a drone
van, a public relations team, and a
school bus full of children wearing
orange scarves. Q rode in the first
SUV with Beto. Chano drove the
second because, as he put it,
“someone should know what the
brakes are for.”
At the reserve entrance, a woman in
a wool shawl stopped them. She
was small, old, and held a wooden
staff polished by use.
“The cameras stay outside,” she
said.
plates.caption: A future above breakfast.
plates.scene_brief: Beto's tablet projects a single artificial butterfly over the motel breakfast table; Q studies the itinerary and Chano watches Beto. This is a promotional hologram rendered as grayscale light, not a real forest.

plates.facing_text:
Beto smiled. “We have
authorization.”
“From whom?”
He named the foundation.
The woman looked at Q. “And
you?”
“I have cameras for seeing,” Q said.
“I can stop them retaining or
transmitting images. Would that
meet the rule?”
She asked the technician
accompanying the school group to
check the indicator. He did, and Q
showed him how the recording
setting differed from ordinary
vision.
The woman stepped aside. “Stay
with the guide.”
The cameras remained outside.
Beto remained with them, though
he claimed this was a strategic
choice.
The forest climbed around the
visitors. Sunlight crossed the
oyamel branches in narrow shafts.
Monarchs gathered in clusters that
bent the smaller limbs; where they
stirred, orange broke through the
darker folded wings.
The children fell silent.
Even Chano removed his cap.
Q had read accounts of their
navigation and the succession of
generations on the journey north.
He had expected the scale to be
difficult to convey. What he had not
anticipated was the sound when a
patch of folded wings opened
beside his head. He stopped
describing them to Chano.
The woman waited until they
moved again. “There are more on
the other side of that tree. Stay on
this path.”
Q made room for a child to see. For
several minutes he forgot to
consider how he would report the
visit to the Custodian.
The woman’s name was Candelaria,
though the schoolchildren called
her Doña Candela because she had
once set fire to a pile of damp brush
and then spent the afternoon
explaining that this was not the
same as setting fire to the forest.
She had guarded the reserve for
twenty-six years. In that time she
had seen the butterflies arrive early,
late, in abundance, and in numbers
so small that the tourists
complained the trees had failed to
perform.
At the boundary of the visitor area,
where Beto rejoined them without a
camera, she told him, “They are not
here for the tourists.”
“The tourists support the reserve.”
plates.caption: He stopped describing them.
plates.scene_brief: Q steps aside for a child to see monarchs clustered on a low oyamel bough; Chano has removed his cap and Candelaria leads on the marked path. No camera crew in the restricted forest.
plates.scene_anchor: Q made room for a child to see.

plates.facing_text:
“The tourists support the road, the
restaurants, the guides, and the
people who rent cabins. The reserve
supports the butterflies.”
“Those interests can be aligned.”
“They can also be confused.”
She described the year a fire
crossed the western slope. It began
in a field where a man had burned
the remains of a harvest. The fire
was not large at first. A wind
changed direction. Someone called
the municipal office. Someone else
called the forest brigade. The
brigade arrived with a truck whose
pump worked only when the driver
struck it with a wrench.
The tourists were evacuated. The
cabins were saved. The trees on the
slope burned.
“Were you able to compare the next
arrival with the year before?” Q
asked.
“In three groves. The fourth was the
one that burned.”
“Did the report keep that
distinction?”
“The screen doesn't have an empty
space. Watch.”
The foundation later described the
fire as a resilience event. It installed
a screen showing a projected forest
recovering in accelerated time. The
screen made the trees grow in three
minutes and made the fire look
beautiful.
Candelaria refused to stand beside
it.
“Did they ask you to approve the
recovery figures?” Q asked.
“They asked me to stand beside the
screen. I was carrying buckets that
week.”
She took a smaller group along the
working path to the burned slope.
The children stayed with their
teacher except for a girl whose
mother was coming to water a tree.
The path was narrow, and the fallen
needles covered stones that shifted
underfoot. Chano went ahead,
testing the ground with a branch.
Beto stayed behind because his
shoes were designed for
presentation rather than descent.
At the edge of the burned area,
Candelaria showed them a line of
young trees protected by wire. Each
tree had a small tag bearing a
number. The foundation had
planted them as part of a
reforestation campaign. Beside the
wire, local families had planted
other trees without tags.
“Which ones will survive?” Q asked.
“The ones someone waters.”
Q read the tags and asked who was
doing the watering. The listed
plates.caption: Trees someone waters.
plates.scene_brief: Candelaria shows Q wire-protected saplings beside untagged family plantings on the burned slope. Chano tests the loose path with a branch. No miraculous recovery or delivered hose.

plates.facing_text:
subcontractor was based in
Morelia. Its contract had ended the
previous month.
“The dates stop here,” he said. “Has
anybody taken over?”
“Three families. They use their own
cans. We have asked for the hose
back.”
Q noted the hose as something he
could ask the foundation about. It
would be possible to do that
without offering an interpretation
of the entire forest.
The girl in the orange scarf carried
a small blue bucket and wore boots
two sizes too large.
“My grandfather planted that one,”
she said, pointing beyond the wire.
“How long have you been watering
it?” Q asked.
“Since he hurt his foot. It has his
name.”
She whispered the name to the tree.
Q did not hear it and did not ask
her to repeat it. The little blue
bucket was empty before the earth
looked wet.
“Another?” he asked.
“We filled it at the bottom.”
Q looked back down the slope. “I
could bring a larger container.”
“There's a wheelbarrow,” her
mother said. “Try it on this path.”
He looked at the stones. The larger
container could wait for the hose.
Chano took the bucket for the
return walk; Q carried the child's
coat while her mother tightened a
loose wire around the young tree.
The girl instructed her to leave
room for it to get fat. Her mother
said she was trying to do the same
for her.
Candelaria led them farther uphill.
From there, the reserve appeared as
a patchwork of cabins, milpas,
roads, roofs, and forest. A new
zip-line had been planned across
the valley. Its brochure showed
visitors passing through a cloud of
butterflies while a guide explained
the importance of leaving no trace.
“Will it disturb them?” Q asked.
“The company says no.”
“What do you say?”
“I say their report counted visitors
in July. Ask to see the dates.”
Q opened a reminder for the report.
The contradiction was one he could
check.
The assembly below had begun to
argue about the corridor.
Candelaria watched the people
gathering beneath the canvas roof.
“The forest is not an example,” she
said. “It is a place where people
plates.caption: Room to grow.
plates.scene_brief: The watering girl's mother adjusts loose protective wire around the sapling, leaving growing room; Q holds the coat and Chano the small blue bucket. The child wears oversized boots. She is not automatically Lidia, Micaela or the grieving girl.

plates.facing_text:
have to decide what they will do
tomorrow.”
Q looked at the butterflies moving
through the branches. Their motion
seemed random until he observed it
over time. Then it seemed
patterned until a gust of wind broke
the pattern. He could describe both
impressions and trust neither as the
whole truth.
“Do you read the reports people
write after coming here?” he asked.
“Some. There is usually more about
their feelings than our work.”
Q thought of the paragraph forming
in his journal. “I may owe you a
hose before I owe you a
description.”
“The foundation owes us the hose.
You can remind them.”
They caught up with the girl and
her mother where the working path
rejoined the visitor route. Chano
was still carrying the blue bucket.
He declined the teacher's invitation
to join a race to the next bench.
Q looked up. A butterfly landed on
the silver question mark stitched to
his jacket. Its wings opened and
closed against his chest.
One girl began to cry. Her teacher
knelt beside her.
“My mamá says they remember the
dead,” the girl said. “My abuela
brought me here last time.”
Q had been ready to answer a
question about navigation. He let
that answer go. The teacher made
room for the girl on a fallen trunk.
Q moved back so the others could
sit beside her.
A boy asked him why he was so
quiet.
“There is quite a lot to listen to.”
“I thought you were charging.”
“If I could do that by standing in a
forest, I would save a fortune.”
The girl laughed through her tears.
Then she began to tell the teacher
about the shoes her grandmother
had worn. Q listened without
adding a better ending.
When they stood to go, the butterfly
lifted from Q's jacket and crossed
above the teacher's head.
Candelaria checked the time.
“They will have started without us.”
They followed her to a clearing
where twelve people sat beneath a
canvas roof. Some were farmers,
some teachers, some forest guards.
A young man held a tablet with a
cracked screen. An older woman
had brought a ledger bound in blue
cloth. It lay open beside a plate of
tortillas.
plates.caption: The shoes her grandmother wore.
plates.scene_brief: The teacher and classmates sit beside the grieving girl on a fallen trunk. Q has made room and listens while a monarch rests on the stitched question mark of his jacket. No apparition, robotic embrace or conversion of the child into a symbol.

plates.facing_text:
Q waited at the end of a bench until
the woman with the blue ledger
waved him over. She was reading
back the previous meeting's
decisions. A man interrupted to say
he had not promised his truck, only
to ask his brother about it. She
changed the entry. The brother,
who was sitting beside him, said he
had not been asked. They moved on
before he could decide whether to
be offended.
“The corridor surveyors came
again,” said the young man with the
tablet. “They say the road will bring
jobs.”
“They say the same thing every
time,” said the woman with the
ledger.
“This time they have drones.”
“Last time they had lawyers.”
“Before that they had rifles.”
No one laughed.
Q listened. The dispute had no
clean villain. The corridor might
bring money, clinics, and roads. It
might also divide the forest, lower
water tables, and make the
community legible to people who
believed legibility was a form of
ownership. Each argument made
the others worse by being partly
true.
“You can solve this,” Beto said
quietly. He had joined them at the
clearing, carrying a tablet in place
of the camera he had left outside.
Q asked the woman with the ledger
whether she wanted help
comparing the route maps. She
consulted the others. The young
man with the cracked tablet wanted
to know why two maps gave
different distances to the spring.
“Show us that,” he said. “Don't
decide which road we want.”
Q placed the maps beside one
another. The foundation's line
ended at the edge of a parcel. The
residents' line continued to the
spring itself. That accounted for
part of the difference; an old path,
absent from one map, accounted
for the rest. He marked the
discrepancy and asked the young
man to check it.
“Can your system keep all this
together?” the woman asked.
Q described a model that could
compare route lengths, slopes, and
estimates of water use. He began
adding employment forecasts to the
list. Beto nodded. Q found himself
explaining how it might organize
later decisions as well.
“Can we remove it if it is wrong?”
Candelaria asked.
plates.caption: Two distances to the spring.
plates.scene_brief: Q and the young man compare two route maps at the canvas-roof assembly: a parcel endpoint differs from a spring endpoint. The ledger keeper listens. No political vote tally or invented accurate geographical labels.
plates.scene_anchor: Q placed the maps beside one another.

plates.facing_text:
“You should be able to. Let me
check what happens to the maps.”
The foundation's package charged
for access to the underlying maps
after the trial. Q checked the export
terms. The reports could be
downloaded; the layers needed to
change them could not.
“You could keep the pictures, but
you couldn't correct the route
without paying. I wouldn't
recommend that arrangement.”
“The subscription includes
support,” Beto said.
“We have support,” said the man
who had not lent his brother's
truck. “We are discussing whether
it will start.”
The woman closed the blue ledger.
“Then leave us the maps.”
The meeting continued. The canvas
had been borrowed from the
primary school; the benches had
been carried up after a faena
repairing the forest road. Atole
passed in enamel cups. Two men
who wanted the new road disagreed
about where it should enter. A
woman who opposed its present
route offered the visitors more
tortillas before returning to her
argument.
The minutes were read in Spanish.
At a disputed boundary, a
Mazahua-speaking elder and the
secretary checked a place-name
together. Q could identify the
language more readily than he
could follow their exchange. He
waited for the secretary's version
and marked the boundary as
disputed.
The group assigned people to meet
the surveyors, inspect the northern
path, and check the distance to the
spring. The final three lines
remained unsigned. Q did not have
to decide whether that meant
agreement. The secretary told him
they had not finished.
Beto waited until the benches were
being carried away.
“At least show them the possible
positions,” he said. “For
discussion.”
The young man agreed to a
comparison by sector, without
names. Q looked again at the
northern path. One sector
contained a single house.
“That would still identify the
household,” he said. “And I can't
turn what people said into votes.
You can want the road and object to
this route.”
“I do,” the young man said. “I also
want to stop talking about it before
dark.”
Q proposed a list of the
measurements still needed. The
plates.caption: The disputed boundary.
plates.scene_brief: A Mazahua-speaking elder and the secretary consult the map together at the assembly. Q waits for the secretary's version rather than pretending fluency. Atole, working benches and the blue ledger keep the setting practical. Do not invent indigenous script or ceremonial dress.
plates.scene_anchor: the secretary checked a place-name together.

plates.facing_text:
young man took his paper and drew
two columns himself. One was for
the foundation's distances, the
other for the distances they would
check on foot. He left the second
empty.
“Those blanks will look bad in the
presentation,” Beto said.
“Then don't take them to the
presentation,” the woman with the
ledger said.
They checked the headings and
kept the sheet with the minutes. Q
had no tally of political positions to
export. Beto photographed the
empty benches instead and
described the consultation as
completed.
The young man saw the post while
folding the canvas. He asked Q to
hold the other end; there was more
wind than canvas and Beto had
already reached the car.
“Completed,” he read. “Will that
make them stop coming?”
“I doubt it. Shall I ask him to say
the measurements are still
pending?”
“Ask him to bring two people to put
this up next time.”
Candelaria added that the next visit
was a path inspection, not another
meeting. Q sent both points. For
the first time that afternoon his
message was shorter than the work
it described.
Beto was already on the telephone
about a model town and a
candidate with high trust potential.
Chano heard his own name.
“Candidate for what?”
“A community appointment,” Q
said. “Apparently the breakfast
governorship has acquired an
office.”
Chano laughed once. No one joined
him.
Afterward, the woman with the
ledger approached Q.
“You read a great deal,” she said.
“A great deal. Not enough about
these parcels.”
“Will you come back when they
inspect the path?”
“If you want me there.”
“We want somebody who saw that
the surveyors were told it was
disputed.”
She gave him the inspection date
and asked whether he needed it on
paper.
“The reminder should work.”
“Bring boots that do too.” She
looked at his feet. “Or whatever
those need.”
plates.caption: Consultation completed.
plates.scene_brief: Q and the young man fold the broad borrowed canvas against the wind while benches are removed. Beto is already by the car. Physical comedy, no triumphant completed-agreement ceremony.
plates.scene_anchor: He asked Q to hold the other end;

plates.facing_text:
That afternoon, Beto arranged a
recording in the permitted visitor
area below the forest. He placed Q
beneath a tree and asked him to
speak about hope. The finished
video would cut between this scene
and licensed footage of monarchs.
Q began with the broken watering
arrangement. Beto asked for
something broader. Q supplied a
polished statement about
knowledge, technology, and a
shared future. The foundation
approved it before anybody had
checked the hose.
While Q spoke, Chano noticed a
child at the edge of the frame. She
held a cardboard sign with a
question written in marker: WHO
WILL ASK THE
BUTTERFLIES?
The production team cropped her
out.
The next morning Q withdrew his
approval of the edit. The longer
recording showed what had
interrupted him and why his first
answer had concerned a hose. It
also showed the child. He kept that
version off his public account and
asked the teacher to put him in
touch with her family.
Lucía relayed the teacher's
suggestion: KEEP THE SIGN.
REMOVE THE CHILD. Q asked
whether the child and her mother
wanted that. They watched a
private preview cropped to the
cardboard, without the child's face,
voice, uniform or name. Her
mother agreed to its use in the
report of the visit. The girl asked
him not to correct the uneven
letters. Q said they were better than
his.
He published that version, with the
family's limits attached. It became
more popular than the polished
speech. The foundation copied it
into an education package and
proposed an exhibition. By then Q's
report was only one of several
places where the question could be
found.
Three days later the mother asked
for the recording to come down.
People at school knew whose sign it
was. The permission had not made
its consequences easy to predict, or
obliged the family to enjoy them.
Q removed his upload and sent the
changed request to the foundation.
“We already removed her,” Beto
said.
“They want the recording removed
now, including the question.”
“They agreed to the question.”
“I know. I'm the person they told.
They've told me something else.”
plates.caption: Leave the letters as they are.
plates.scene_brief: Lidia and her mother review the private cardboard-only crop beside Q. The screen contains no child's face, name, voice or uniform. This is the limited approval conversation, not unauthorized filming. Keep lettering indistinct; caption is separate.

plates.facing_text:
Beto called it a betrayal. Mar called
it a pivot. The foundation called its
lawyers.
Mar sent him the addresses of two
publishers who had taken the
package. Q contacted them with the
mother, keeping his own removal
separate from the copies they had
not yet reached. Candelaria's hose
was still on his list. He called about
that too, before drafting an
explanation for the Custodian.
Interlude: The Butterfly
That Entered the
Dashboard
The child who had made the
butterfly sign was named Lidia. Q
knew her name from the
permission conversation; it had not
gone into the report. When her
mother came to the foundation's
office, the original upload was
already down. The education
package still played the cropped
cardboard beneath Q's voice.
The office occupied a renovated
hacienda at the edge of the reserve.
Its walls were adobe-colored, its
windows were bulletproof, and its
gift shop sold butterfly ornaments
made in factories too far away to be
visited by tourists. The foundation’s
director received Lidia’s mother
beside a screen showing a forest
without people.
“We protected your daughter’s
identity,” the director said.
“Her class made the signs,” the
mother replied. “They know which
one she made.”
“You approved this version.”
“And now she gets asked it on the
bus. Every morning.”
Q stood beside the screen. An
animated butterfly had been added
to the edge of the cardboard. It
landed on the question mark every
eleven seconds. Neither the family
nor Q had been shown this version.
“My report is down,” he said. “This
copy is yours to remove.”
The director silenced it. The
butterfly continued landing.
The director offered compensation
in the form of school supplies, a
reserve membership, and a family
pass to the foundation’s new
immersive exhibit.
“We do not want a pass,” the
mother said.
“The offer is intended as
recognition.”
“Recognition is what caused this.”
The director glanced at Q. “Perhaps
the machine can explain the
protection protocol.”
Q brought up the family's changed
request instead. It had a date and a
plates.caption: The butterfly keeps landing.
plates.scene_brief: The foundation director silences the screen while Q and Lidia's mother watch the animated butterfly still visible beside the cropped cardboard. Office setting and power imbalance; no actual butterfly indoors or claim the mother approved this later version.

plates.facing_text:
list of the copies they knew about.
The director's assistant found one
more in a teacher training pack.
She added it to the list before her
employer could explain why it was a
different use.
“All of those,” the mother said. “Do
I have to come back for each one?”
“Not to tell me,” the assistant said.
“I can send the same request.”
Lidia entered carrying the
cardboard sign. The paint had run
where the rain had fallen. The
letters were still legible:
WHO WILL ASK THE
BUTTERFLIES?
The director brightened. “We can
include the physical sign in the
exhibit.”
“No,” Lidia said.
“It would be behind glass.”
“People can still read it.”
“The question has entered public
conversation.”
“I want to ask something else.”
Q asked what she wanted to ask.
“Whether we can go. I have a
match.”
Her mother checked the time. The
bus they needed left in twenty
minutes. Q asked the assistant for a
copy of the request and a number
they could call without making the
journey again.
Q searched the distribution logs.
The video had been mirrored by
schools, media outlets, a ministry
portal, and a company selling
air-quality monitors. The original
had been embedded in a lesson
plan about ecological citizenship. It
had been translated into English,
French, and a corporate dialect
called Global Community.
“Removal cannot be guaranteed,” Q
said.
“Neither can protection,” the
mother replied.
The director stood. “We have acted
in good faith.”
“Then nobody needs to be offended
when they change their minds,”
Chano said.
He had been waiting by the door
with a paper receipt for the school
supplies the foundation had
offered. He handed it back.
“The supplies are useful,” the
director said.
“Then give them to the school
without attaching her name.”
“That would weaken the impact.”
“The school can survive the loss.”
Lidia placed the sign on the desk.
“Keep the cardboard.”
plates.caption: She has a match.
plates.scene_brief: Lidia holds the wet cardboard while her mother checks time and Q asks the assistant for a receipt and contact. Distinct director and assistant. Lidia's impatience, not a grand symbolic gesture, organizes the scene.

plates.facing_text:
The director hesitated.
“We may use it as a symbol,” she
said.
“No. You can keep it because it is
wet and I do not want it in the
house.”
The director accepted the sign as
though receiving an artifact. Q
watched her label it DONATED
OBJECT: UNKNOWN MINOR.
“That is not the name,” Lidia said.
“It protects you.”
“I'm standing here.”
Q reached for the label maker.
“What should it say?”
Lidia thought for a moment. “It
should say that I do not want it
used.”
Q entered the sentence. The label
maker retrieved QUESTION
RETAINED, IMAGE
WITHDRAWN from the video's
old catalog entry.
“That's the old request,” Lidia's
mother said.
Q cancelled the label and wrote on a
piece of paper:
DO NOT DISPLAY OR
REPRODUCE. FAMILY
REQUESTS REMOVAL.
The mother read it. “Attach it to the
record as well. Otherwise they will
lose the paper.”
The director brought a lawyer in
from the next office. He argued that
the sign had been donated in a
public building, that Q had
appeared in the footage under a
public contract, and that the
question had acquired independent
cultural value.
“Independent of whom?” Chano
asked.
The lawyer looked at Lidia.
“Independent of its original
context.”
“Her permission was for a report of
the visit,” Q said. “Where did the
exhibition become part of it?”
The lawyer turned to him. “You are
not qualified to assess cultural
value.”
“I'm asking which agreement you're
using.”
The director said they could make
an appointment for further
discussion. Lidia's mother had
already made one for this
discussion. She opened her bag to
find the confirmation, then shut it
when the assistant handed her the
receipt for the removal request.
plates.caption: The old request.
plates.scene_brief: Q cancels the old label template and writes the family's changed request on paper while the mother watches. Cardboard lies on the desk, not transferred to an exhibition. No invented readable legal text.

plates.facing_text:
“That's what I need. Send the
answer there.” She pointed to the
contact field.
Q held the door while Chano
checked where the bus stopped.
There was no need to remain until
the director agreed that they had
been reasonable.
Lidia retrieved the sign. The
cardboard bent at the center,
leaving the question in two halves.
She folded it again and carried it
out beneath her arm.
That evening, the foundation
released a statement praising the
family’s participation in responsible
media practice. The statement used
the phrase question retained,
image withdrawn, taken from
the earlier catalog entry. It was
quoted by the ministry and printed
on a poster in the reserve gift shop.
The assistant sent an answer the
following week. The training pack
had been replaced and the office's
screen no longer played the
recording. Two outside publishers
had not replied. The poster
remained in the gift shop, where it
was now classified as a statement of
institutional policy.
Q asked Lidia's mother whether she
wanted him to follow up with the
two publishers. She did. She also
asked him not to send progress
reports during school hours: the
phone was hers, and she was trying
to get some work done.
He changed the time of his next
message. Beneath the reminder he
kept a second question for when
they next spoke: how the match had
gone. That one did not need to go to
the foundation.
Interlude: The Tianguis of
the Unregistered
On the morning after the office
visit, Q and Chano drove down to
the next town. The tianguis there
was raising money to repair the
road. Tarps stretched between two
mesquite trees above cheese, pan
de pulque, honey, clay pots,
wooden toys, and bags of seeds
bearing names written by hand.
Micaela had fastened a sign to a
table: ASK BEFORE YOU SCAN.
She had made it from a cereal box.
The students who arrived with a
tablet read the sign. One asked the
seed seller whether she wanted her
stall included in their survey.
“Will it bring customers?”
“It may help us arrange the stalls
next time.”
“Then include me. I want the corner
by the bus.”
Celestina, unfolding a cloth over
her basket of tortillas, wanted the
plates.caption: The next bus.
plates.scene_brief: Q holds the office door open as Lidia and her mother leave, the folded cardboard under Lidia's arm. Chano checks the way to the bus stop. No guard confrontation and no Q blocking the exit.

plates.facing_text:
same corner. The student explained
that no place had been promised.
Both women asked her to write
down the request anyway.
“You could share it,” Q said.
“We could,” Celestina agreed. She
pulled her table six inches toward
the bus stop.
The student, whose name was Vero,
showed them the form. It asked for
a name, a portrait, products, prices,
and an estimate of takings. The
seed seller would give her products
but not her prices. Celestina would
give neither her face nor her
takings. She had a photograph in
which she looked better than the
one Vero was likely to take, but did
not see why selling tortillas
required either.
Vero disabled the camera and left
those fields blank.
“Will it let you finish?” Q asked.
She submitted a test entry. The
form accepted it. Nothing alarming
happened. The seed seller asked
whether this meant she had the
corner.
Vero's partner was counting people
at the entrance. A boy ran past him
carrying a stack of empty cups,
returned without them, and ran
past again with a sack of sugar. On
the third passage the student
lowered his pencil.
“Are you buying anything?”
“Not until they pay me.”
Q had a suggestion about counting
arrivals. Before he could offer it,
Celestina put a packet into his
hands and pointed out its customer.
He spent the next quarter of an
hour carrying purchases toward the
bus stop. On the fourth trip the boy
with the cups told him to ask about
his wages too.
Rain started at the cheese stall and
reached the rest of the market in
time for everyone to claim they had
predicted it. The seed seller lifted
her bags onto an empty crate.
Celestina covered the tortillas.
Chano took a pole from beside the
cooperative store and pushed up
the sagging center of a tarp.
Water slid off onto the table Q had
just cleared.
“Was that the plan?” he asked.
“It is now. Hold this.”
Q took the pole. Chano went to help
the boy carry the sugar indoors. The
rain made a drumming sound so
much larger than its drops that Q
turned toward it. A cold thread ran
beneath his cuff. He raised the
sleeve clear of his wrist joint and
stayed where Chano had put him.
Micaela moved the sign into the dry
space at his feet.
plates.caption: Hold this.
plates.scene_brief: Rain at the tianguis: Q holds the tarp pole where Chano asked him to stand; Micaela moves her cereal-box sign into the dry patch at his feet. Chano carries sugar toward the store with the working boy. No phone-photo dispute or injured robot.

plates.facing_text:
“You're in the way.”
“If I move, the roof follows.”
She considered this and set her
backpack beside the sign. Several
other people found room for
something under his patch of tarp.
By the time Chano returned, Q was
keeping a basket, three schoolbags
and a sleeping dog dry.
“I thought you were going to look at
the market,” Chano said.
“It has come to me.”
Chano secured the pole to the table
frame with a rope. Q let go
cautiously. The dog opened one eye
and closed it again.
Vero's partner brought the count
over. It showed fewer customers at
the inner tables, several of which
were now empty. He thought the
next tianguis should put its most
popular sellers there to draw people
through.
“Those tables were full before the
rain,” Celestina said.
“There wasn't anyone buying when
I counted.”
“Their stock is in the store.” She
pointed across the road. “So are
their buyers.”
Q walked over with him. A woman
was measuring honey into a jar on
the shop counter while two
customers waited. They brought
her table back when the rain eased.
The student crossed out his
proposed stall move and wrote the
time of the shower beside the
count.
The seed seller wanted another
covered area. Celestina wanted the
road repaired first, so the bus could
reach the market after more than a
shower. There was not enough in
the collection tin for either. Vero
turned the tablet so they could see
the sponsor's offer: payment for
completed vendor profiles, with a
larger amount for profiles that
included portraits and sales figures.
“I told them we were studying the
market,” Vero said. “That's what
our project is called.”
“They should come on a day like
this,” Chano said.
“Our supervisor did. He left before
the rain.”
“Experienced man.”
The vendors gathered around the
tin. Some wanted to supply the
extra fields. Others did not. One
woman offered a photograph of her
pots; a man asked whether he could
send the portrait from his wedding
because he had paid for it already.
Vero showed them which fields
were optional and what each
version earned.
plates.caption: The buyers went inside.
plates.scene_brief: Inside the cooperative store, a woman measures honey into a jar for waiting buyers; Q and Vero's male partner look in from the entrance, his tally sheet lowered. Wet market visible outside. Commerce has relocated, not vanished; no rescue or invasive photo.

plates.facing_text:
Q asked whether the sponsor would
fund a count of stalls, products and
busy hours instead. Vero had sent
that proposal the previous week.
She opened the reply for him:
useful for the students' report, but
not eligible for the larger payment.
“Then there's no need to send it
again with my name on it,” Q said.
“The reply might be faster.”
“It would be difficult to make this
one shorter.”
Celestina wanted no profile. The
seed seller agreed to a list of
products, without prices. Other
stallholders made different choices.
Vero recorded them separately.
Micaela turned her sign toward the
late arrivals. The marker had run in
the rain; she borrowed Vero's
pencil and went over the last word.
The road collection remained short.
The man who kept the tin said they
would hold another sale the
following month. Celestina looked
at the seed seller.
“You can have the corner next time
if you bring a tarp.”
“For both tables?”
“Now you want to share.”
At the end of the afternoon, the
students had a count they could
explain and less funding than their
supervisor had expected. No one
had taken Celestina's photograph.
The seed seller packed the unsold
bags. Vero's partner put away his
tally sheet and began carrying
tables to the cooperative store.
Micaela tried to put the sign in her
backpack. It would not fit until she
bent a corner.
“You'll need that again,” Q said.
“Then you can carry it.”
He took it. Chano said it was the
first useful souvenir he had
acquired.
Celestina left a tortilla folded in
four for the student who had stayed
to take down the tables. He ate it
and asked whether she would be
back next week. She said to bring a
rope if he was coming; one of the
tarps had nearly torn loose.
Music came from the room above
the store. Q stopped beneath the
stairs to listen while the student
swallowed the last of the tortilla.
“They take requests,” the boy said.
“Do they take visitors?”
“Ask Tere. She'll give you
something to carry.”
He took the other end of the table.
plates.caption: Music above the store.
plates.scene_brief: At market closing, Q pauses beneath the stairs to listen to music from above while the student takes the other end of a table. Celestina's tortilla and Micaela's awkward sign remain ordinary working objects, no ceremonial presentation.
plates.scene_anchor: Q stopped beneath the stairs to listen

plates.facing_text:
Interlude: The Station
That Did Not Broadcast
Everything
The following morning, Tere let Q
and Chano into the radio room
above the cooperative store. She
had invited them to help examine
an offer of new equipment. Q had
also asked whether he might stay to
hear a broadcast. The antenna was
fastened with wire to a water tower,
and the microphone had been
repaired so many times that no one
knew which of its parts still
belonged to the manufacturer.
They called it The Voice of the
Sierra, although the sierra did not
speak on the radio. The teachers
spoke, and farmers, and women
announcing an illness, and children
asking for a song, and men
reporting that the road was closed
by a landslide. Some notices lasted
ten seconds. Others occupied an
hour because no one had yet found
a way to end the argument.
A sustainable-innovation
foundation offered a new system. It
could record every broadcast,
transcribe it, translate it, and use it
to build a map of community needs.
In exchange, the station had to
permit the Castalia archive to
preserve the recordings
indefinitely.
“What does needs mean?” Tere, the
operator, asked.
“What people request,” said the
representative.
“People request songs.”
“They are cultural data as well.”
“They request that someone return
a mule.”
“That is logistical information.”
“They request that someone stop
beating his brother.”
The representative paused.
“That is sensitive information.”
“Everything that matters becomes
sensitive when a company records
it.”
Q sat beside the transmitter with
the terms open. He had been
invited to explain them and had
arrived with an alternative indexing
scheme as well. He recognized the
habit before opening the second
document.
“Which parts do you want to be able
to replay?” he asked.
“And who decides what is a notice?”
Tere asked.
“You would have to. The software's
category is only a guess.”
“The system does not know when a
woman is asking for help and when
she is testing the microphone.”
plates.caption: The station above the store.
plates.scene_brief: Tere and Q review equipment terms in the radio room above the cooperative store; Chano and the representative nearby. Patched microphone, transmitter and ordinary notebooks. No magical archive or omniscient map.

plates.facing_text:
“Then you need a switch that can
leave a conversation out of the
recording,” Q said. “Where do you
keep the instructions from callers?”
Tere pointed to the radio table.
There were three notebooks:
WHAT MAY BE REPEATED,
WHAT MAY BE HEARD
ONCE, and WHAT DOES NOT
GO ON AIR.
“The station decides,” she said.
The representative smiled.
“The station is a small institution.
The system will give you capacity.”
“The capacity to remember is not
the capacity to decide.”
A boy entered with a sheet of paper.
He had written the names of five
songs his uncle had recorded and
the time he wanted them played.
“I want you to play this,” he said.
Tere looked at the list.
“Did your mother give permission?”
“It is not my mother’s. It is my
uncle’s.”
“And him?”
“He is chopping wood.”
“Then ask him.”
The boy went out. The
representative looked at the clock.
“We have a demonstration
window.”
“The window does not know the
uncle,” Tere said.
The first broadcast of the day was a
notice about water. A woman spoke
in Spanish, stopped, and asked the
operator to call her daughter so she
could continue in the family
language. Tere switched off the
recorder during the call. The
representative protested.
“If we do not record it, we lose the
context.”
“It was not your context.”
“The community loses an
opportunity to be understood.”
“The community is not a school
assignment.”
Q consulted the system board. The
broadcast was recorded as AUDIO
INTERRUPTED BY PRIVACY
CONDITION.
“Does the interruption log retain
anything from the call?” Q asked.
Tere looked at the board. They
checked it together. It kept the time
and the duration. Q showed her
how to turn that logging off for
private calls too.
At noon, the radio broadcast the
notice about the missing mule. A
man gave the animal’s name, the
color of the saddle, and the road
where he had seen it. Then he
added a sentence unrelated to the
plates.caption: A call outside the recording.
plates.scene_brief: Tere switches off the recorder while helping the caller contact her daughter; Q checks the logging control beside her. Do not depict a waveform recording the private call or legible contact data.

plates.facing_text:
mule: his brother had come back
from the north without speaking to
anyone.
Q marked the mule notice for
replay, then paused over the last
sentence.
“Keep that part out,” Tere said. “He
rang to ask about the mule.”
“Does he want a separate message
about his brother?”
“I'll ask him when he comes for the
shopping.”
Q removed the final sentence from
the replay queue. The
representative pointed out that the
missing context reduced the value
of the entry.
“The entry is for finding a mule,” Q
said. “It still does that.”
That afternoon, the foundation
projected the map of needs onto the
wall of the store. It showed orange
points where the radio had received
the most calls, green lines where
farmers had mentioned roads, and
a red zone the system identified as a
concentration of conflict.
“The red zone is the court,” said a
young man.
“That is where the children play,”
said another woman.
“The system detected many
complaints.”
“Because the visiting team
cheated.”
“The model does not know the
difference.”
Q opened the sample behind the
red zone. It contained an argument
about a visiting football team. The
classifier had treated the word
dispute as evidence of a land
conflict.
“This isn't a disputed parcel,” he
said. “That point should come out.”
“We can improve the model with
additional data,” the representative
said.
The assembly fell silent. The
representative interpreted the
silence as interest.
“We can improve the map with
more recordings.”
“You can make it worse with more
certainty,” said Candelaria.
She had come down from the
reserve with her cane and a
notebook. She opened the notebook
and showed the names of trees
without labels.
“You've put the court in a dispute
that will be sent to the
municipality,” she said. “Who takes
it out before the next report?”
The representative said the
foundation could not erase data
without preserving a reason.
plates.caption: The visiting team cheated.
plates.scene_brief: Residents and Q examine a disputed projected needs-map marker at the store. A nearby ordinary football court explains the argument behind the label; do not portray armed land conflict, a real national map or a scientifically verified classification.

plates.facing_text:
“Then preserve the reason,”
Candelaria said, “but not the data.”
Q looked at Tere. The station had a
proposal prepared: thirty days for
public recordings, no recording of
private calls, and permission for
transcripts.
A teacher objected to the thirty
days. Her class used last year's
rainfall notices to compare the
roads that had closed. Tere turned
to a fresh page.
“Which notices?”
The teacher had brought a list. They
agreed to ask the speakers about
keeping those broadcasts longer. Q
offered to help find the dates in the
station's existing index. Tere
accepted, provided he did not
reorganize it while looking.
“I had a suggestion,” he admitted.
“It can go in the fourth notebook.”
There was no fourth notebook.
Chano offered to sell him one.
Songs would remain outside the
Castalia archive unless their owners
offered them for that purpose.
“That reduces the value of the
archive,” said the representative.
“It reduces the value you can
extract,” Tere replied.
“History will be lost.”
“History is not the same as your
record.”
The boy returned with his uncle.
The man wiped his hands on his
trousers and read the list of songs.
“The first one may go on,” he said.
“The others may not.”
Tere marked the single-song
permission in the station notebook;
it included no deposit with Castalia.
She played the song on air. The
uncle sat beside the transmitter and
listened to his own song as if it had
arrived from a place he still did not
know how to name.
Q switched off the index for that
broadcast.
The representative entered LOSS
OF CULTURAL ASSET in his
report. Tere entered the uncle's
instruction beside the title and
turned up the speaker. He leaned
forward to hear a passage he had
played himself. Q stayed for the end
of it.
At dusk, the radio broadcast the
state of the road, the price of corn, a
recipe for curing children’s fright,
and the mule’s name, for it had
returned on its own. No one knew
whether the man’s brother would
speak again.
Q checked that the mule notice was
no longer in the replay queue. Tere
told him the man would collect his
plates.caption: His own song.
plates.scene_brief: The uncle leans forward beside the transmitter to hear his own performance; Tere raises the speaker and Q stays to listen. Nephew nearby. The broadcast is permitted without a Castalia deposit; no Q performance, archival transfer or supernatural music.
plates.scene_anchor: Q stayed for the end of it.

plates.facing_text:
shopping in the morning. There
was no reason for Q to stay and find
out what happened with the
brother.
Before leaving, he wrote where to
find the logging switch in the
station's maintenance notebook.
Tere tried it, then asked him to put
the description of the button above
the explanation of why it mattered.
He did. She gave him the times of
two programs he might like.
During the evening call, Q told the
Custodian about the rainfall
records and the station's proposed
terms. The Custodian asked how
much of that belonged in their
chapter.
“Less than I've just told you, I
think. I haven't told you about the
market.”
He began with the two women who
wanted the same corner. By the
time he reached the rain, Chano
was standing beside him correcting
the account of the pole. Q had made
it sound as though he had
volunteered.
“You said hold this. I held it.”
“And I said I'd be back.”
“The dog had begun to doubt you.”
The Custodian asked about the dog.
Q started that part again, more
slowly.
The Road to the
Appointment
In the morning, Beto sent the
address of the model town and a
schedule which left no time for
anything to go wrong before the
official photographs. Chano read it
twice. Then he asked Q to keep the
forest inspection date clear of the
new appointment. Apparently a
governor also needed permission to
have a day off.
Q put the two dates beside one
another. The hose still needed
following up; Lidia's family had not
received every answer; Tere's
program began while they would be
on the road. He set a reminder for
that too.
At the mirror above the motel
basin, Chano examined his chin.
“Should I shave?”
“For you or the photograph?”
“I was hoping I could do both at
once.”
Q waited while he found the razor.
plates.caption: Both at once.
plates.scene_brief: Morning motel basin: Chano examines his chin in the mirror before the official appointment, razor among ordinary washing things; Q waits beside him in the fitted jacket. Reflect Chano correctly; no Custodian physically present, office already reached or imposed knightly costume.
